sentiment.rationale: The document reports a strong backward-looking quarter (revenue beat, $11B Blackwell ramp), but forward guidance is cautious: gross margin is guided to a trough of 71% (down from 73.5%) with a back-loaded recovery promise, growth decelerates sharply from 114% to ~65% YoY, and tariffs are explicitly called 'an unknown.' The Q&A reveals management hedging on margin recovery and policy risk, which lowers forward expectations. The score is negative because the forward outlook is materially weaker than the prior trajectory, despite the headline beat.

summary.revenue: Q4 revenue $39.3 billion, up 12% sequentially and 78% year on year. Full fiscal 2025 revenue $130.5 billion, up 114% from prior year.
summary.guidance: Q1 (next quarter) revenue expected to be $43 billion, plus or minus 2%. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins expected to be 70.6% and 71%, respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points. Full-year fiscal 2026 operating expenses expected to grow in the mid-30s.
summary.margin: Q4 non-GAAP gross margin 73.5%, down sequentially. Q1 guided to 71% non-GAAP. Management expects gross margin to return to mid-70s late this fiscal year.
key_risks: Gross margin trough during Blackwell ramp, with recovery back-loaded and unproven.
Tariffs explicitly described as 'a little bit of an unknown' with no quantification.
China data center sales remain at about half of pre-export-control levels and are expected to stay there absent regulatory change.
Networking revenue declined 3% sequentially during product transition.
Gaming revenue declined 22% sequentially due to supply constraints.
key_opportunities: Blackwell ramp is the fastest product ramp in company history, with $11 billion revenue in first full quarter.
Three scaling laws (pretraining, post-training, inference time) driving demand for AI computing.
Enterprise data center revenue grew nearly 2x year on year.
Automotive vertical revenue expected to grow to approximately $5 billion this fiscal year.
New products (Blackwell Ultra, Vera Rubin) on annual cadence.

management_tone.label: mixed
management_tone.justification: Management expresses strong confidence in the Blackwell ramp and long-term AI demand ('Demand for Blackwell is extraordinary'), but simultaneously hedges on margins ('we have many opportunities to improve the cost... but right now we are going to focus on getting the manufacturing complete') and explicitly flags tariff uncertainty ('it's a little bit of an unknown').
